narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 62% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That means failure was judged more likely than passing, not certain, and the decision followed from that risk estimate. The strongest factor pushing toward failure was your third-year class standing: you were in the third decile, while accepted students averaged about the sixth decile. Your family-income bracket, upper-middle, was the second most influential factor and also added to the estimated risk, although many accepted students share that bracket. Your first-year class standing was third in influence: a third-decile position, compared with an accepted average near the sixth decile, again pushed toward failure. Your LSAT and undergraduate GPA were below accepted averages, but they were less influential than those three factors. Gender and race were not used. To strengthen a future application, seek admissions feedback, retake the LSAT if you can improve, submit updated grades or additional coursework showing readiness, and consider schools or programs whose admission thresholds better match your profile. A pre-law advisor can help you build an updated application that directly addresses the academic concerns the model flagged.
